question.question: What determines Vagabond rolled hits and defenseless status, do exhausted swords count, and how are excess hits handled?

expected.expected_answer: Rolled cap is all undamaged swords in Satchel face up or down. Exhausted undamaged swords count. Defenseless defending if no undamaged swords. Each hit damages one undamaged item; ignore hits after all undamaged items gone.

source_passages.quotation: - **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.

Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Boots/swords/crossbows/torch/hammers are gained face up in Satchel. Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.ruling: As attacker or defender, Vagabond’s maximum rolled hits equal all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down. Thus an exhausted but undamaged sword counts; a damaged sword does not.
Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords.
Each hit damages one undamaged item of the Vagabond’s choice. Ignore excess hits when no undamaged items remain.
